source.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
source.scope: Reviewed the complete article and footnotes, including the private held-out dataset, log-perplexity trend, proposed common limits and explicit exclusions for post-training, chain-of-thought and an unknown entropy floor.
source.freshness_reason: Selected after a complete source read, a current lane comparison and explicit treatment of evidence limits.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete article and footnotes, including the private held-out dataset, log-perplexity trend, proposed common limits and explicit exclusions for post-training, chain-of-thought and an unknown entropy floor.

stories.summary: OpenAI’s Jakub Pachocki proposes using prediction loss on a private held-out text distribution as a common signal for pacing pretraining progress. The post reports falling log-perplexity across model generations and argues that labs could coordinate around shared limits before monitoring matures. The measure is not a complete intelligence score: data mixtures differ, post-training and chain-of-thought sit outside it, practical task gains can diverge, and the irreducible prediction floor remains unknown.
stories.why_it_matters: A common measurement can support coordination only if labs can compare procedures without leaking evaluation data or treating one curve as all capability. Track the dataset protocol, uncertainty, model-family comparability and the milestones that would justify changing any proposed limit.
stories.image_alt_intent: Separate laboratory prediction-loss curves approach a shared safety boundary while side panels flag private datasets, post-training exclusions and an unknown entropy floor.
stories.related_coverage: Chosen over newer discussion posts because the original proposal contains the measurement definition and its limitations.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete original architecture report, its shared-block loop design, claimed effective scale, coding emphasis and the disclosed tendency toward overly long marathon-thinking loops.

stories.summary: Z.ai describes GLM‑5.4 as its first flagship Loop Transformer, repeatedly executing a shared block so reasoning depth can rise without adding a new set of parameters at every step. The company frames coding as a general problem-solving substrate and reports performance comparable with much larger parameter counts. Those are first-party claims, and the post discloses a practical failure mode: repeated reflection can become unusually long even when it improves accuracy.
stories.why_it_matters: Repeated depth changes the operating question from model size alone to how much inference time a task is allowed to consume. Evaluate completion quality, latency, loop length, tool stability and cost on your own coding workloads before adopting the claimed effective-scale comparison.
stories.image_alt_intent: A compact transformer block loops through repeated reasoning passes while gauges compare parameter count, inference time, coding accuracy and runaway reflection.

source.title: Prompt caching
source.scope: Reviewed the complete current documentation for cache creation and read counters, exact-prefix matching, the tools-system-messages hierarchy and model-specific invalidation behavior. The page exposes no reliable publication date.

stories.summary: Anthropic’s prompt-caching documentation explains that cache creation, cache reads and uncached input are reported as separate token counters. Reuse depends on an exact matching prefix across tools, system content and messages; changing an earlier layer invalidates the layers that follow. Thinking blocks and tool changes can introduce model-specific invalidation behavior. The documentation is operationally useful but undated, so it supports a current procedure rather than a fresh product-announcement claim.
stories.why_it_matters: Before blaming a quota or billing system, log all three token counters and compare the serialized prefix byte for byte. Change one component at a time, preserve stable tools and system text, and verify that a second request produces cache-read tokens.

stories.headline: Insert a human summary checkpoint before an agent’s final verification

source.title: The Software Atelier
source.scope: Reviewed the complete 294-passage source transcript and reading edition, including Ronacher’s own session data, project-maintenance limits, executive-summary checkpoint, interoperability warning and suspendable-runtime proposal.
source.freshness_reason: Selected after a complete source read, a current lane comparison and explicit treatment of evidence limits.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete 294-passage source transcript and reading edition, including Ronacher’s own session data, project-maintenance limits, executive-summary checkpoint, interoperability warning and suspendable-runtime proposal.

stories.summary: Armin Ronacher argues that stronger models have changed how far coding agents can run even when the underlying harness stays similar. His own sessions show longer runs and many projects started, while sustained human attention remains scarce. He inserts a readable executive-summary checkpoint before final verification so the operator can redirect a bad tradeoff before more work accumulates. The talk reports one practitioner’s workflow, not a controlled benchmark.
stories.why_it_matters: For one bounded coding task, require the agent to stop before final verification and produce a short HTML summary of the goal, files changed, tradeoffs, unresolved risks and proposed checks. A named reviewer must approve, redirect or cancel before the agent resumes.
stories.image_alt_intent: A long-running coding agent pauses at a human review gate, presenting a concise change summary, tradeoffs and unresolved risks before final verification resumes.
stories.related_coverage: Selected as the edition’s only Agent Skills story after novelty comparison and complete transcript review.
